www.text: The Nashville Jewish Film Festival, created as a forum to help the wider local community understand the complexity of issues surrounding contemporary Jewish life, will host its opening night celebrations this evening.
Ofir Akunis, Israel’s consul general in New York, is slated to address the Sephardic Rabbinic Conference during its final day in New York City.
The Rocky Mountain Jewish Historical Society at the University of Denver is hosting Yeshiva University’s Rabbi Stuart Halpern today for a talk on his book Jewish Roots of American Liberty.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s Likud party is holding its primaries across Israel today.

Hawaii’s Gov. Josh Green is working to secure state and federal recovery resources after Hurricane Lala (since downgraded to a tropical storm) resulted in major flash floods and widespread power outages and road closures, with search-and-rescue operations underway.
The second annual Sephardic Rabbinic Conference kicks off today in New York City, bringing together over 150 rabbis and communal figures. Read more about it below.
The Docu.Text Festival kicks off on Sunday at the National Library of Israel in Jerusalem.

Parents, alumni and other stakeholders of Camp Lavi are continuing their efforts to prevent the camp from being sold to another organization, launching a crowdfunding campaign that has so far raised more than $2.3 million.

The Mamram Alumni Association, which unites veterans of the Israel Defense Forces’ elite computing unit, will host an invitation-only founders meetup today at Google in Tel Aviv, featuring a fireside panel with Israeli Mapped in New York’s Guy Franklin.
Jewish relief groups are beginning to provide emergency response services following the 7.4 magnitude earthquake that struck western Colombia earlier this week…

The Greater Miami Jewish Federation launched an emergency relief fund after a 7.4 magnitude earthquake in western Colombia on Monday rocked more than 20 municipalities across the country, killing more than 100 people. In a post on X, Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Sa’ar offered the Colombian government “any assistance that Israel can provide.”

Tomorrow afternoon in Israel, the Jewish Theological Seminary will present President Isaac Herzog with an honorary degree at a ceremony at the President’s Residence in Jerusalem, formalizing a degree awarded to him in May.
A federal bankruptcy court in New Jersey will meet today to review a new plan for the sale of Camp Lavi in Lakewood, Pa. More on this below.

gifts.text: The Lake Worth Playhouse, Palm Beach County’s oldest theater, secured a $1 million anonymous gift to seed an endowment that will fund repairs to its 103-year-old building…

B’nai B’rith Israel has joined a campaign to fund the rehabilitation of released hostage Evyatar David. More than 2 million NIS ($680,000) has been raised toward a 3 million NIS ($1.02 million) goal to cover his long-term medical, psychological and related recovery needs…

The family of Sgt. 1st Class Shahar Gamla, an Israel Defense Forces officer killed by an explosive drone in Lebanon in June, donated his organs to save six lives, among them 7-year-old Bel Finkelstein, who received a liver lobe transplant at Clalit-Schneider Children’s Medical Center…
Conservative donors Liz and Dick Uihlein committed $35 million over three years to Northwestern University’s football program…

A three-year, $430,000 grant from The Leon Levine Foundation will underwrite the first executive director, early programming and student leadership roles at Clemson University‘s new professionally staffed Hillel, which will launch this fall after years of being a student-led operation…
The OpenAI Foundation is committing $100 million to a new program that will use AI tools to expand access to advanced medical treatments for underserved patients…

Samantha and Scott Johnson donated $1 million to Jewish Nevada — the largest security gift in the organization’s history — to fund guards and local grants, bolster statewide coordination via the Secure Community Network, and establish a $100,000 matching initiative to inspire additional community giving…

Philanthropist David Rubenstein gifted the Anti-Defamation League an archival pigment print of the stone engraving of the Declaration of Independence, which is now mounted in the lobby of its New York offices…

Rice University trustee Patti Lipoma Kraft and her husband, Jonathan Kraft, the president of The Kraft Group, have given a gift to fund the university’s football practice pavilion as well as endow the Kraft Family Professorship in Jewish Studies…

The Gates Foundation awarded $540 million to the University of Washington’s Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation — the largest charitable gift in the university’s history — to expand its Global Burden of Disease study over a 10-year period…

Investor Michael Moritz‘s Crankstart Foundation, with the nonprofit Lever for Change, launched a global competition offering $10 million to $50 million each to up to three organizations for workable plans to improve life in San Francisco…
